sentences.text: Hello and welcome to the Slow English podcast. My name is Emili. I am very happy you are here today.
In this episode, we will travel to Seoul, the capital of South Korea. Seoul is a modern,
exciting and historic city. It is full of lights, people, technology and traditions.
Today, let's explore Seoul together in slow and easy English. Are you ready? Let's begin.
Part 1. Where is Seoul? Seoul is in South Korea, in East Asia. It is the capital and the largest city
of the country. About 10 million people live in Seoul, but the wider area has more than 25 million
people. This makes Seoul one of the biggest cities in the world. Seoul is in the northwest of South
Korea, near the Han River. The river runs through the city and gives it a beautiful view.
Part 2. The climate Seoul has four clear seasons. Spring is mild and full of cherry blossoms.
Summer is hot and rainy. Autumn is cool, dry and colorful with red and yellow leaves.
Winter is cold with snow and ice. The seasons make the city beautiful and different at each time of
year. Part 3. A short history. Seoul is very old. People have lived in this area for more than 2000
years. It became the capital of Korea in the 14th century during the Joseon dynasty.
In the 20th century, Korea was divided into North and South. Seoul became the capital of South Korea.
Today, Seoul is a modern city with technology, skyscrapers and culture. But it also keeps its history
alive with palaces, temples and traditional houses. Part 4. Palaces and History. Seoul has many old
palaces from the Joseon dynasty. The most famous is Jeonbokkung Palace. It is big and beautiful,
with traditional Korean architecture. Other palaces include Chiangdokkung and Deoksugung.
Visitors can watch the royal guard changing ceremony at the gates. These palaces show the
long history of Korea. Part 5. Modern Seoul. Seoul is very modern. It has tall skyscrapers,
neon lights and busy streets. Areas like Gangnam, Myungdong and Dongdaemon are full of shops, cafes
and entertainment. Seoul is also famous for technology. Big companies like Samsung, LG,
and Hyundai are based in South Korea. In Seoul, you can see the latest technology everywhere.
Part 6. The Han River. The Han River is very important to Seoul. It flows through the city and gives
people space for sports, parks and festivals. Along the river, you can see people cycling,
running and picnicking. At night, bridges light up with colorful shows. Fireworks festivals
happen by the river and many families enjoy it together. Part 7. Korean Culture.
Seoul is the heart of Korean culture. Traditional music, art and food are everywhere.
But modern pop culture is also very strong. K-pop is world famous.
Bands like BTS and Blackpink come from Seoul. There are music shows, concerts and shops selling
K-pop goods. Korean dramas called K-dramas are also popular worldwide. Many are filmed in Seoul.
Part 8. Food in Seoul. Korean food is delicious and unique.
Some famous dishes are kimchi, spicy fermented cabbage eaten with almost every meal.
Bibimbap, a bowl of rice with vegetables, meat, egg and chili sauce.
Bulgogi, marinated beef cooked on a grill.
Ttebaki, spicy rice cakes, a popular street food.
Samgyebsal, grilled pork belly eaten with lettuce and sauces.
Street food in Seoul is very popular. At markets like Guangzhou Market, you can try pancakes,
dumplings and noodles. Part 9. Traditional houses.
Seoul has special old houses called Hanoq. They are wooden with curved roofs and small courtyards.
You can see Hanoq in the Boogchon Hano village. Many Hanoq are now cafes, guest houses or museums.
Walking there feels like going back in time.
Part 10. Shopping in Seoul. Seoul is great for shopping.
Mayangdong is famous for fashion and cosmetics.
Namdaemun Market and Dongdaemun Market sell clothes, food and souvenirs.
COEX Mall is one of the biggest shopping malls in Asia.
People from all over the world come to shop in Seoul.
Part 11. Nature in the City. Even though Seoul is big, it has nature too.
There are mountains around the city, like Boogchon San. People love hiking there on weekends.
There are also many parks, such as Namsan Park, with the famous N Seoul Tower.
From the tower, you can see the whole city.
Part 12. Festivals and events.
Seoul has many festivals. In spring, the cherry blossom festival is very popular.
In summer, there are music festivals.
In autumn, people celebrate the Seoul Lantern Festival, with colorful lanterns by the river.
In winter, there are lights, Christmas markets and ice skating.
These festivals make the city alive all year round.
Part 13. Transportation.
Seoul has one of the best metro systems in the world.
The subway is clean, safe and very big. It is easy to travel everywhere in the city.
There are also buses, taxis and trains.
From Seoul, you can travel to other cities in Korea very quickly.
Part 14. Daily life.
People in Seoul are busy. They study hard, work long hours and travel quickly.
But they also love food, music and spending time with friends.
Cafes are everywhere. People enjoy coffee, tea and desserts and stylish cafes.
Some cafes even have cats, dogs or books.
At night, Seoul never sleeps.
Shops and restaurants stay open very late.
Part 15. Why visit Seoul?
So, why should you visit Seoul?
Because it has everything, history and old palaces,
modern buildings and lights, delicious food and street snacks, nature, mountains and parks,
music, kpop and culture, friendly people and exciting life.
Seoul is a city of energy, color and stories.
It is a place where tradition and the future live together.
Outro. That is all for today's episode of the Slow English Podcast.
We learned about Seoul, the capital of South Korea.
It is a city full of history, culture, technology and beauty.
A city that welcomes visitors with open arms and delicious food.
I hope you enjoyed this journey and learned new words in English.
